title: Continuous and perfect tenses in the passive
intro: Read this before the questions on the continuous and perfect passive.

blocks.title: the pattern
items: **Continuous tenses add BEING:** be + **being** + past participle.
**Perfect tenses add BEEN:** have + **been** + past participle.
The last word is always the past participle. The passive adds exactly one form of be: is, **is being**, **has been**.

blocks.title: continuous passive
items: **Present continuous:** am / is / are **being** + past participle: The road **is being repaired**. (Active: They are repairing the road.)
**Past continuous:** was / were **being** + past participle: The room **was being cleaned** when I arrived. (Active: Someone was cleaning the room.)
**Negative and question:** The road **isn't being repaired**. **Is** the road **being repaired**?

blocks.title: perfect passive
items: **Present perfect:** have / has **been** + past participle: The letter **has been sent**. (Active: Someone has sent the letter.)
**Past perfect:** had **been** + past participle: The film **had been cancelled** before we arrived.
**Future perfect:** will have **been** + past participle: The work **will have been finished** by Friday.
**Negative and question:** It **hasn't been sent**. **Has** it **been sent**? Only the first helper moves.

blocks.title: rare forms
items: The future continuous passive (*will be being done*) and the perfect continuous passive (*has been being done*) are very rare. Choose the present perfect passive or another structure instead.
Do not mix the two: *has being sent* and *is been repaired* are wrong.
